subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should OpenClaw make compact, goal-shaped browser reads the default behavior, and what explicit raw/full escape hatch should remain for workflows that need complete page state?
rationale: Current main has caps, efficient mode, and generic truncation, but changing the default model-facing browser read contract affects agent behavior and compatibility in a way automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Compact Default With Raw Escape Hatch
options.body: Make the default snapshot/read path compact and actionable, keep explicit full/raw AI or ARIA reads for complete refs, and validate both paths with browser plugin tests plus live proof.

options.title: Keep Efficient Mode Opt-In
options.body: Leave current defaults intact and document mode=efficient, maxChars, selector reads, and pruning as the supported workaround for context-heavy browser tasks.

options.title: Fold Into Browser Field Report
options.body: Track the remaining decision under the broader browser automation field report if maintainers want one umbrella for action diffs, stale refs, viewport reads, and context shaping.

recommendation.title: Compact Default With Raw Escape Hatch
recommendation.body: Make the default snapshot/read path compact and actionable, keep explicit full/raw AI or ARIA reads for complete refs, and validate both paths with browser plugin tests plus live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The browser plugin boundary and core ownership history make this the best available product-contract owner signal.
